literal: Like the hand of one who lost his garment, immediately removing distress is friendship.
translation: True friendship is that which instantly rushes to remove a friend's distress, just like the hand of a person whose garment slips off.
modern: ஆடை நழுவியவனுடைய கை உடனே சென்று மானத்தைக் காப்பது போல, நண்பனுக்குத் துன்பம் வந்தபோது உடனே சென்று அத்துன்பத்தைப் போக்குவதே நட்பாகும்.
explanation: This couplet uses a vivid and powerful analogy to define true friendship. When a person's garment slips, their hand acts instantly and instinctively to cover them, without any hesitation or conscious deliberation. Similarly, when a friend falls into distress, a true friend does not wait to be asked or hesitate, but immediately rushes to remove that suffering. The word 'āṅkē' (immediately) emphasizes the instantaneous nature of this help, and 'iṭukkaṇ kaḷaivatu' highlights that friendship is defined by active relief of distress.
